name: Battle of Agincourt

phases.title: The two armies are drawn up
phases.text: The English stood in three groups across the defile, with archers on the flanks and men-at-arms in the centre. The French stood in a vanguard and a main battle behind it, with dismounted men-at-arms in the wings, cavalry on the flanks of the vanguard and a mounted rearguard.

phases.title: The English move up and shoot first
phases.text: Henry ordered his army forward and the stakes were pulled up and set again in the new position. The English longbowmen then shot from extreme range, and the French cavalry charged only after this first volley.

phases.title: The French cavalry charge the archers
phases.text: The French cavalry, disorganised and not at full numbers, charged towards the longbowmen. They could not outflank the archers because of the woodland, and could not charge through the stakes.

phases.title: The wounded horses break back through the French
phases.text: The charge failed and the cavalry fell back. Wounded and panicking horses galloped through the advancing infantry, scattering and trampling it, while the vanguard walked on through the mud.

phases.title: The French men-at-arms reach the English line
phases.text: The surviving French men-at-arms reached the front of the English line and pushed it back, while the longbowmen on the flanks went on shooting at close range. When their arrows ran out the archers attacked the French with hatchets, swords, spears and mallets.

phases.title: The second line joins and the fight is lost in the press
phases.text: The French second line joined the attack but was swallowed up, the narrow ground hampering it. The fighting lasted about three hours, until the leaders of the second line were killed or captured, as those of the first line had been.

note: The precise location of the battle is not known, and the directions are not given. The woods stand either side of the narrow open land; the accounts do not say exactly where they lay. The English stood across about 750 yards of the defile, so the plan is not to scale. The English account places the baggage attack at the start of the battle and some accounts place it near the end; it is left off the plan. The plan shows the English archers 'left' and 'right' as drawn here: the accounts do not say which of the two wings each stood on.
